title: tecoma radicans var. atropurpurea
intro: Tecoma radicans var. atropurpurea, commonly known as the Coral Honeysuckle, is a variety of the coral honeysuckle plant native to the southeastern United States. It is a woody vine known for its clusters of bright red, orange, or yellow flowers, which are a valuable source of nectar for hummingbirds and other pollinators. The Coral Honeysuckle has been traditionally used in herbal medicine to treat various health issues, including fever, sore throats, and respiratory problems, due to its health benefits of reducing inflammation and acting as an expectorant. The bioactive constituents of Tecoma radicans var. atropurpurea include flavonoids, alkaloids, and phenolic acids, which are responsible for its therapeutic actions of anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties.
